text:
monitoring-bot: 🚨 High backend error rate and 6x origin QPS spike for /generate (hosted) since 13:23 UTC. Cache miss rate jumped from 8% -> 74%. Latency p50 -> 420ms, p95 -> 1.8s. Trace: small set of hot prefixes.

Alex Kim: who saw this first? is it KV-store flaking or a change this morning? :eyes:

Marta L.: saw alerts 13:24. Rolling retention shows a sharp drop in prefix hit-rate around 13:20. No infra deploys at that exact time but config push to runtime happened at 13:15 (batching heuristics + key-normalization).

Ryan C.: attaching quick profiler dump and cache metrics snapshot. Key observations:
- hit_rate by prefix: many top prefixes went from 95% -> 10%
- eviction churn increased ~5x (cache thrash)
- kernel selection latency climb correlated with longer seq lengths when miss penalty incurred (KV fetch adds ~100-200ms and we fall back to unoptimized path).

Leo (sre): repro steps I ran:
```
# simulate hot prefix storm
export PREFIX="How do I reset my password"
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST $API -d "{\"prompt\": \"$PREFIX $i\"}" &
done
```
Result: origin QPS spikes and cache add rate huge -> eventually origin CPU saturates.

Tana (oncall): suggestion: consider emergency disable of prefix cache for hosted tier while we diagnose. We can flip a feature-flag in ~2m. Thoughts?

Alex Kim: ok hold on -- before disabling, do we know root cause? Marta, what did the config push change in keying?

Marta L.: the change normalized whitespace and removed trailing punctuation from prefix keys to improve hit rates for small edits. But I missed that it also strips certain non-ascii tokens (we use tokenizer normalization fallback) — that produced a different canonicalization for prefixes containing emojis and non-ascii apostrophes. A lot of traffic from mobile clients includes curly quotes -> keys mismatched with warm caches that were keyed with old normalization. So misses.

Ryan C.: + batching heuristic change increased the default max_batch_tokens from 1024 -> 2048 for a small subset of routes. That made requests pack longer prefixes before hitting kernel fast path; on a miss we couldn't benefit from fused kernels and the cost per miss blew up. Combo of key mismatch + larger batches -> eviction + long tail.

Alex Kim: ok that explains it. Disable caching for affected route makes sense to stop origin overload while we roll a fix. Tana, do it and post deploy id.

Tana (oncall): disabling prefix cache for /generate in hosted-prod now. Deploy: deploy-2026-03-17-13:36. Flipping flag... done. :white_check_mark: TTLs will still expire but no new cache writes.

E2E-bot: smoke tests: all green. Traffic back to baseline in ~90s. p95 dropped to 320ms.

Alex Kim: good. Next: quick rollback plan and permanent fix options. Marta, can we roll back the normalization change or make it backward-compatible?

Marta L.: plan A: revert normalization change (fast). Plan B: add dual-key writes for 12 hours (write both old and new key forms) so pre-warmed entries still hit. Plan C: keep new normalization but run a short async pre-warm job for top N hot prefixes. I can push plan B as a config toggle.

Ryan C.: also propose immediate batching tweak: revert max_batch_tokens for those routes to 1024 and enable kernel-path enforcement on misses so we don't trigger slow path. That's a runtime flag, low risk.

Leo (sre): operational mitigations: 1) rate-limit worst offending prefixes with token-bucket per-prefix, 2) add jitter to cache TTLs to avoid synchronized expiry, 3) add request coalescing (singleflight) so parallel misses for same prefix wait on one origin fetch. We should do singleflight in front of origin - cheap and helpful.

Alex Kim: prioritize: 1) dual-key writes (Marta) 2) batching revert (Ryan) 3) singleflight (infra). Marta and Ryan, can you get PRs out in the next 30m? I'll own the rollout and QA.

Marta L.: PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4291 (dual-key write toggle, default off). Includes opt-out and metrics to count dual hits.

Ryan C.: PR opened: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4292 (revert per-route max_batch_tokens change + kernel-path flag).

Alex Kim: testing plan: deploy to canary first (canary has smaller traffic but same clients), run synthetic hot-prefix generator (Leo's script), confirm hit-rate improves and origin QPS stable, then roll to hosted-prod with staged population.

infra-bot: canary deploy queued -> canary-2026-03-17-13:58.

Leo (sre): notes from profiler after canary: hit_rate for top prefixes recovered to ~92% with dual writes, eviction churn reduced, origin CPU back to normal. Kernel-path enforcement prevented fallback that added 120-180ms per miss.

Alex Kim: great. Action items recorded:
- Marta: enable dual-key writes (toggle) in prod for 12h, monitor hit_rate and disk usage.
- Ryan: revert batching for routes, add kernel-path enforcement flag.
- Infra: implement singleflight in front of origin cache (next sprint if can't patch in hotfix).
- SRE: add TTL jitter and per-prefix token-bucket limit.

Marta L.: enabling dual-key writes now. Will monitor metrics and revert if unexpected growth.

Tana (oncall): re-enabled server-side prefix cache writes at 14:04 with dual-write toggle on. Observed gradual warm-up of hits and origin QPS trending down.

Alex Kim: postmortem notes (initial):
- Root cause: normalization change produced incompatible key form for many mobile-origin prefixes + batching heuristic change increased miss cost.
- Contributing: lack of dual-write/backcompat strategy for key changes, TTL alignment (many keys expired simultaneously), no singleflight for hot-prefixes.
- Immediate mitigations: emergency disable, dual-key write roll, revert batching.
- Long-term: require keying change checklist: dual-write support or migration window, add automated canary of key changes, implement singleflight and jittered TTLs, expand perf tests to include miss-path kernel latency.

Alex Kim: I'll kick off the postmortem doc after we stabilize. Thanks all for the quick turnaround. :trophy:

monitoring-bot: Incident resolved at 14:12 UTC. Total incident duration ~49m.
